articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped fixes for 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Because apparently April showers bring security flowers, or something equally catastrophic.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vulnerability is getting hammered in the wild with ransomware crews already capitalizing on millions of potentially exposed sites. The backbone of the internet is once again made of graham crackers.

articles.title: cPanel drops patches for exploited authentication bypass zero-day
articles.summary: Watchtowr drops their trademark snark on the cPanel authentication bypass CVE-2026-41940 that's currently making hosting providers everywhere question their life choices. 'The Internet Is Falling Down' indeed.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military hackers are exploiting router vulns to mass-harvest Microsoft Office tokens because apparently your ancient Linksys is now a state-sponsored espionage tool. Who could have seen this coming?

articles.title: Polymarket Rejects Data Breach Claims as Hacker Alleges 300K Records Stolen
articles.summary: A 15-year-old allegedly pwned France's entire ID agency and tried hawking millions of citizen records on the dark web. The kids are definitely not alright, but their OPSEC game is strong.

articles.title: Hackers are actively exploiting a bug in cPanel, used by millions of websites | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sri Lanka just disclosed they've lost over $3 million in separate cyber incidents while recovering from economic crisis. When it rains, it pours government treasury funds into hacker wallets.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: FOIA requests exposed the dystopian reach of ALPR surveillance, so naturally states are now trying to block public records access. Transparency is apparently only good until citizens actually see what's happening.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's anti-VPN law goes live next week because nothing says 'freedom' like forcing citizens to browse the web naked while the state watches. Time to dust off those Tor bridges, folks.

articles.title: If AI's So Smart, Why Does It Keep Deleting Production Databases?
articles.summary: North Korea now controls 76% of all stolen crypto in 2026, turning digital heists into a national industry with possible AI assistance. The DPRK's economy is basically one giant ransomware operation at this point.

articles.title: A Bridge to Somewhere: How to Link Your Mastodon, Bluesky, or Other Federated Accounts
articles.summary: Germany just doxxed 'UNKN,' the mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware operations, revealing 31-year-old Daniil Shchukin's face to the world. Another legend falls to operational security failures and persistent law enforcement.
